readme.content:
# hn-mcp-server

An MCP server that exposes Hacker News as tools and resources — callable by any MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code).

Built with the official Python `mcp` SDK. No API keys required.

---

## Demo

![Tools List](screenshots/tools_list.png)

![Tool Call and Response](screenshots/tool_call_and_response.gif)

---

## MCP Primitives

### Tools

| Tool | Description | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `get_top_story` | Fetch top N HN stories by score | `count: int = 10` |
| `get_story_details` | Full details of a single story | `story_id: int` |
| `search_hn` | Search HN via Algolia by keyword | `query: str`, `count: int = 10` |

### Resources

| URI | Description |
|---|---|
| `hn://top` | Top 5 HN stories as plain text context |

![Resource Read](screenshots/resource_read.png)

### Prompts

| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| `hn_briefing` | Morning briefing prompt — instructs the LLM to fetch and summarize top stories |

---

## Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/eshitakundu/hn-mcp-server
cd hn-mcp-server
python -m venv venv

# Windows
venv\Scripts\activate

# macOS/Linux
source venv/bin/activate

pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Test with MCP Inspector

```bash
mcp dev server.py
```

Opens the MCP Inspector in your browser. From there you can list tools, call them with arguments, read resources, and inspect the raw JSON-RPC messages.

---

## Connect to Claude Desktop

Add to `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` (Windows) or `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hn-server": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["C:\\full\\path\\to\\hn-mcp-server\\server.py"]
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude Desktop. You can now ask Claude:

- *"What's trending on Hacker News today?"*
- *"Search HN for anything about AI agents"*
- *"Give me details on story 12345"*

Claude will call your tools automatically and use the results in its response.

---

## APIs Used

| API | Usage | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| [HN Firebase API](https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/) | Story data, top story IDs | None |
| [Algolia HN Search](https://hn.algolia.com/api) | Full-text search | None |

---

## Stack

- Python 3.11+
- [`mcp`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk) — official MCP Python SDK
- [`httpx`](https://www.python-httpx.org/) — HTTP client

entrypoint_file.content:
import httpx
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
from datetime import datetime

mcp = FastMCP("hn-server")

HN_BASE = "https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0"
ALGOLIA = "https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1"

@mcp.tool()
def get_top_story(count: int = 10) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Fetch top N stories from Hacker News on the basis of score.
    """
    with httpx.Client() as client:
        response = client.get(f"{HN_BASE}/topstories.json")
        story_ids = response.json()[:count]

        stories=[]
        for story_id in story_ids:
            r = client.get(f"{HN_BASE}/item/{story_id}.json")
            data = r.json()
            stories.append({
                "id": story_id,
                "title": data.get("title"),
                "url": data.get("url"),
                "score": data.get("score"),
                "by": data.get("by"),
                "comments": data.get("descendants", 0)
            })
        return stories
    
@mcp.tool()
def get_story_details(story_id: int) -> dict:
    """
    Get full details of a single HN story including comment count and metadata.
    """
    with httpx.Client() as client:
        r = client.get(f"{HN_BASE}/item/{story_id}.json")
        data = r.json()
        return {
            "id": story_id,
            "title": data.get("title"),
            "url": data.get("url"),
            "text": data.get("text"),  
            "score": data.get("score"),
            "by": data.get("by"),
            "time": datetime.fromtimestamp(data.get("time")).isoformat(), 
            "comments": data.get("descendants", 0),
            "type": data.get("type")
        }
    
@mcp.tool()
def search_hn(query: str, count: int = 10) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Search Hacker News stories by keyword using Algolia.
    """
    with httpx.Client() as client:
        r = client.get(
            f"{ALGOLIA}/search",
            params={"query": query, "tags": "story", "hitsPerPage": count}
        )
        data = r.json()
        results = []
        for hit in data.get("hits", []):
            results.append({
                "title": hit.get("title"),
                "url": hit.get("url"),
                "author": hit.get("author"),
                "points": hit.get("points"),
                "story_id": hit.get("objectID")
            })
        return results

@mcp.resource("hn://top")
def top_stories_resource() -> str:
    """
    Top 5 HN stories as readable context.
    """
    with httpx.Client() as client:
        response = client.get(f"{HN_BASE}/topstories.json")
        story_ids = response.json()[:5]

        lines = []
        for story_id in story_ids:
            r = client.get(f"{HN_BASE}/item/{story_id}.json")
            data = r.json()
            lines.append(
                f"- {data.get('title')} (score: {data.get('score')}) "
                f"by {data.get('by')} | {data.get('url', 'no url')}"
            )
        return "\n".join(lines)  

@mcp.prompt()
def hn_briefing() -> str:
    """Morning briefing prompt for HN digest."""
    return (
        "You are a tech news assistant. "
        "Fetch the top 5 HN stories and summarize each in one sentence. "
        "Group them by topic if possible."
    )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
